hero.title: Kids grow up. How do you help them think critically, work things out with others, and find their way in real situations on their own?
paragraphs: Talks with your child, important skills for life, running family and school projects: for children aged 4 to 16 and their parents.
From 15 minutes a day — at home, on a trip, outdoors, with friends.
A ready script: you do not need to invent anything.
hero.cta: Choose a product by the child’s age
hero.leadLink: Or download a trial kit: an advent card, a self-organisation keyring card, and one day of the parents’ calendar.

pain.title: Sound familiar?
items: Your child waits for you to say what to do
Too many clubs, almost no time together
You are not sure they would cope if they got lost or a stranger approached
You worry more than you want to, and you compare yourself with other parents
Your child sometimes finds it hard to talk with other children
Your child always follows other people’s opinions
pain.footer: All of this can be changed. Not with lectures, but with short actions every day.

why.title: Why 15 minutes a day works better than a long weekly class
why.text: A competency is built by repeating a real situation, not by learning a rule. A child takes in what they do next to an adult, not what they listen to. Ten minutes a day fits an evening more easily than one long session a week.

memo.title: Why develop universal competencies?
paragraphs: Grades will not tell you if the child will cope if they get lost. If they can agree without shouting in a conflict. If they can stop when they are angry and understand why it happens.
School teaches subjects. Thinking in a new situation, working things out, holding yourself — it does not. When you are not there, only their competencies remain.
Universal competencies can be developed. Not with lectures, but with short 15-minute practice at home: choose, get it wrong, agree, finish.

abilities.title: What universal competencies are made of
abilities.subtitle: Eight plain phrases. Every kit is built around them.
abilities.literacyLead: And literacy — without it the rest does not work.
abilities.literacy: Universal literacy helps find information, judge it, tell fact from opinion — including on the internet. Subject literacy gives the child basic knowledge about safety, health and money. Example: check whether a chat message is true, or know what to do if they get lost.
abilities.ninth: Independence is not a ninth item on the list. It appears when the others work together.
abilities.ninthNote: A child decides for themselves when they think, take others into account, and manage themselves — at the same time.

approach.title: Our approach
approach.changed: With artificial intelligence and the automation of many processes, the share of routine work is falling worldwide. Work that needs non-standard solutions, critical thinking, the art of communication and emotional intelligence is becoming central — and it needs universal competencies. The main difficulty of today’s world is uncertainty about what will be asked of our children tomorrow. So it is impossible to learn everything in advance: they will constantly have to solve unfamiliar tasks and learn again.
approach.thinking: Analyse a situation or a task, see cause and effect, offer more than one solution when there is no single right answer. Everyday example: why you do not get in a lift with a stranger, but you can with a neighbour.
approach.others: In a world where almost everything happens online, one of the key competencies is being able to communicate. Cooperate, state your view calmly, take the other person’s view into account, settle conflicts so both sides gain. Example: how to share one toy without tears.
approach.self: Understand yourself and your emotions, notice them, not act on autopilot, plan and finish even when motivation and energy have dropped. Example: not throwing the exercise book at a neighbour when something will not work.
approach.literacy: Universal literacy helps find information, judge it, tell fact from opinion — including on the internet. Subject literacy gives the child basic knowledge about safety, health and money. Example: check whether a chat message is true, or know what to do if they get lost.
approach.familyTitle: Why this is the family’s job
approach.family: School teaches subjects. Thinking in a new situation, agreeing, and holding yourself — it does not teach that on purpose. That stays with the family. Not because school is bad. School has a different job.
approach.practice: A short daily practice in a real situation, with an adult, with room to get it wrong. Lectures do not work here. A child takes in what they do themselves.
approach.kits: Each line covers its own competencies. You see that in the tags and the filter. A 24-day advent moves through several competencies. A 14-day kit stays on one, without jumping topics.

aboutPage.title: Who makes RADAR KIDS
intro: We, Julia Gordeeva and Elizabeth Sarycheva, first made these activities for our own families, then decided to turn them into learning kits.

We approached it as professionals: our developers and partners include methodologists, practising and clinical psychologists, teachers, project leaders, internationally certified coaches, and a candidate of pedagogical sciences.

We built a practice system that helps a child grow more confident, able to communicate, and motivated. Along the way the child learns to think critically and find their way in different life situations and a fast-changing world.

sections.title: Who processes the data

sections.title: What we collect
sections.text: On a kit request: name, phone or email, the child’s age, the chosen kit. On a sample request: contact details. On a company request: name, company and role, phone or email, city, date and a rough group size. We do not collect children’s names or medical data on the first form.

sections.title: Why
sections.text: To reply to the request and confirm the format. We do not send a daily newsletter without separate consent.

sections.title: How we store it
sections.text: Requests go to the operator’s email and, if a mail service is connected, to its servers. We keep them while we need to reply, then delete them on request.

sections.title: Your rights
sections.text: You can ask for a copy, a correction or deletion. Write to the contacts on this site. The consent checkbox is required: we do not send the form without it.
